# HPageHeader

> A plain page introduction or the signature atmospheric dashboard hero.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HPageHeader` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-page-header>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthPageHeaderElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Layouts.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HPageHeader.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Use plain for a regular introduction and hero for the atmospheric panel. decoration=false removes the default hero art.
- The component renders h1 by default. Manage the page heading hierarchy when composing multiple headers; the title slot permits deliberate replacement.
- The default slot is the action area. aside adds supporting content.

## Public API

title, accent, description, eyebrow: string · variant: plain | hero · decoration: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    title: string;
    accent?: string;
    description?: string;
    eyebrow?: string;
    variant?: "plain" | "hero";
    decoration?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ variant: "plain", decoration: true }
```

### Events

None

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

title, default (actions), aside

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, eyebrow, title, description, actions

Use `hearth-page-header::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HPageHeader, HButton } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HPageHeader title="Your apps." accent="Right where you left them." description="A home for everything you host." eyebrow="Your workspace" variant="hero">
    <HButton variant="primary">Add application</HButton>
  </HPageHeader>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-page-header');
Object.assign(element, {
  "title": "Your apps.",
  "accent": "Right where you left them.",
  "description": "A home for everything you host.",
  "eyebrow": "Your workspace",
  "variant": "hero"
});
element.innerHTML = "<hearth-button variant=\"primary\">Add application</hearth-button>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.
mount.append(element);
```
